newsitem.title: GERMANY: German retailers say factory outlets kill jobs.
newsitem.headline: German retailers say factory outlets kill jobs.

text.p: Factory retail outlets are job-killers that Germany would be better off without, the HDE German retailers' association said on Thursday.

HDE president Holger Wenzel, alarmed at plans for a 50,000 square metre megastore in Zweibruecken in western Germany, said such centres would destroy city centres and established marketing structures and threaten ordinary retailers.

Even consumers should oppose such American-style centres, where manufacturers offer brand-name goods at prices 30 to 50 percent below downtown stores, because they will reduce competition, HDE said in a newsletter.
"Manufacturers, usually partners of retailers, are leaving their usual place in the chain and emerging as competitors. Worse, they are offering discounts," Wenzel said.
German retailers are subject to strong restraints on discounting, and ordinarily can only cut prices during defined summer and winter sale periods.
The Zweibruecken complex will be far larger than the combined area of Germany's nine current factory-outlet centres, the first of which was built in 1994.
Wenzel said 30 to 50 such centres up to twice as large as Zweibruecken are planned.
